notes.text: Sumo practice at Arashio-beya is NOT confirmed: phone the stable the week before. If there's no public keiko, the fallback is a walk around the Kokugikan, the hand-prints and the statues.
December cold and dark before you leave Sensō-ji. Layers for the Hoppy Street terrace, which is basically outdoors.
Passports all day: tax-free at mita, and ID for the drinking tonight. The omakase TableCheck booking needs a card.

stops.summary: Breakfast is a crawl: tamagoyaki on a stick, grilled scallops, and Kitsuneya's horumon-don eaten standing up.
stops.story: Tsukiji's wholesale market moved out years ago, but the outer market kept the knife shops, the tea sellers and the best street breakfast in Tokyo. Kitsuneya has been simmering offal in the same dark pot for 70 years, and the queue at its tiny counter is half the fun. Go on a cold morning and every grill is steaming.
how: Take the 06:55 Oedo line from Ochiai-minami-nagasaki to Tsukijishijo (¥330, arrives 07:28).
Split into pairs and graze: tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, tuna, uni.
Kitsuneya is a tiny counter, so eat in shifts. Horumon-don or gyudon, bowls about ¥1,000–1,500.
Regroup at 08:30 for the Hibiya line.
tips: Trade buyers have priority until 09:00: step aside for the carts and don't block the aisles.
Kitsuneya is closed Sundays and market holidays. Thursday is safe.
Skip Toyosu's Senkyaku Banrai food hall for breakfast: reviewers say it isn't worth it.
wishes: We love to do it all
Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Real wrestlers slamming into each other before breakfast. Unconfirmed, so CHECK first, with a Kokugikan walk as the fallback.
stops.story: Arashio-beya is a working sumo stable, and for years you could watch morning keiko through the street window: enormous men slapping, shoving and grunting in total silence from the onlookers. Practice viewing is now a course for members of the stable's 俵の会 supporters' club, and the winter tour is at Hasuda on Dec 16, so nothing is guaranteed.
how: CHECK: phone the stable the week before and ask whether there's public practice on Dec 17.
Practice traditionally runs about 7:30–9:00, so arriving at 09:10 you may see only the end. Ask about timing when you call.
If it's on: stand at the window, stay quiet, no flash.
If it's off: walk the Ryōgoku Kokugikan area instead (the arena, the wrestlers' hand-prints, the statues around the station) on your way to the museum.
tips: Silence is the rule: the wrestlers are working, not performing.
Lunch at Chanko Kirishima later keeps the sumo theme going even if practice falls through.
stops.booking: Unconfirmed: phone the stable; viewing is officially a 俵の会 members' course
wishes: Morning sumo practice at a stable (Plan C: Arashio-beya in Ryōgoku) and a private omakase counter
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing

stops.summary: Edo in miniature: walk a life-size Nihonbashi bridge, then a fast loop of the townscape models before lunch.
stops.story: The Edo-Tokyo Museum reopened in 2026 after a long refit, and it's still the quickest way to understand what Tokyo was before the concrete. You walk onto a full-scale chunk of the old Nihonbashi bridge and look down onto tiny Edo streets full of tiny people doing chores.
how: Walk over from Ryōgoku station: it's next to the Kokugikan.
Head straight for the Nihonbashi bridge, then the Edo townscape models.
Keep it to 40 minutes and walk 8 minutes to Chanko Kirishima for 11:30.
tips: There's a Maruyama Okyo special exhibition running through the trip. Skip it today: you don't have the time.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Sumo hot pot from a former ōzeki's house, in your own private room right at opening.
stops.story: Chanko is what sumo wrestlers eat to get huge, and Kirishima's house was founded by a former ōzeki using his Michinoku stable's recipe. Eight of you around a bubbling pot on a cold December day is exactly the right call.
how: Booked: 11:30, private room (個室) for 8. Give the booking name at the door.
Order the house chanko and let the staff run the pot.
Leave by 12:45 for the JR to Uguisudani.
tips: Lunch last order is 14:00, but you're out well before that.
Closed Mondays only, so Thursday is fine.
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: Skip everything else: straight to the swords and armour, Japan's biggest samurai collection.
stops.story: The Tokyo National Museum is huge and you could lose a day in it, so don't. The Honkan's sword and armour rooms are the point: blades that look sharp enough to cut light, and helmets with antlers and demon faces built to terrify people across a battlefield.
how: Enter the Honkan (the main building straight ahead of the gate).
Go straight to the sword and armour rooms. Ignore everything else.
At about 14:25, walk 15 minutes through Ueno Park to Ameyoko.
tips: Ueno Park is bare trees and grey paths in December: walk it briskly, don't sightsee.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Ameyoko's sneaker institution: exclusive collabs and hype pairs. Passports out for tax-free.
stops.story: mita sneakers sits in the Ameyoko Center Building, inside the loud, cramped market street under the train tracks. It's known for exclusive collabs with Nike, New Balance and Asics that you won't find at home.
how: Find the Ameyoko Center Building in the middle of the market.
Go for the mita-exclusive collabs first.
Pay with your passport ready for tax-free.
tips: Tax-free is a refund now: keep the receipt and finish the paperwork at the Haneda T3 customs kiosk on Dec 29.
You have 30 minutes. Decide fast or come back another day.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Sensō-ji before the hall shuts at 17:00, then the year-end battledore fair lighting up at dusk.
stops.story: Hagoita-ichi is Edo's year-end fair: stalls stacked with giant decorated battledores (paddles) covered in kabuki actors and celebrities, sold as good luck for the new year. Buy one and the stallholders do a rhythmic clapping send-off for you right in the crowd.
how: Ginza line to Asakusa, up Nakamise to the main hall before 17:00.
Then work the Hagoita-ichi stalls as it gets dark and the lanterns come on.
Haggle a little, buy one, and get clapped out.
tips: CHECK the fair dates: it's traditionally held in mid-December, but the temple page doesn't list 2026 dates. If it's not on, it's just Sensō-ji at dusk and straight to Hoppy Street.
Small hagoita start from about ¥2,000. The big ones are serious money.
wishes: Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments

stops.summary: Hoppy and beef-tendon stew on Asakusa's oldest drinking street. Pre-game only, the omakase is waiting.
stops.story: Hoppy Street is a row of open-fronted stew bars where old men have been drinking shochu cut with Hoppy, a cheap beer-flavoured mixer, since the post-war years. Okamoto has been there since 1959, seats 100 and can actually fit 8 together on its terrace.
how: Ask Okamoto for the terrace for 8.
Order Hoppy (it comes as a bottle plus a glass of shochu: mix it yourself) and a couple of bowls of nikomi to share.
Leave by 18:50 for the train to Higashi-Nakano.
tips: Don't fill up: there's a ¥22,000 sushi course in two hours.
Ask for 'naka' to refill just the shochu and keep the same Hoppy bottle going.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: The headline: a private omakase counter with just the 8 of you and the chef.
stops.story: Sushi Kunimitsu runs one group per seating, so tonight the whole counter is yours. Piece by piece, straight from the chef's hands: the kind of dinner you talk about for years.
how: Check your TableCheck confirmation: the seating is 20:00 or 20:30.
From Hoppy Street: Ginza line to Kanda, Chuo rapid to Shinjuku, local to Higashi-Nakano, 57 min door to door.
Eat each piece as soon as it's set down, in one bite.
tips: Running late from Asakusa? A taxi takes 36 min. Don't make the chef wait.
No strong perfume or cologne at a sushi counter.
Home: Oedo line 22:53 from Higashi-Nakano to Ochiai-minami-nagasaki (¥180), or a taxi in 11 min.
stops.booking: TableCheck Private Counter Course, late seating, private counter for 8; card required
wishes: Morning sumo practice at a stable (Plan C: Arashio-beya in Ryōgoku) and a private omakase counter
Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)
